prompts.text: We're in a courtroom settling whether cereal counts as soup. Who volunteers as the expert witness?
What completely harmless disagreement deserves the most dramatic legal proceedings?
Putting the last slice of cake on trial or prosecuting someone for never returning a borrowed pen?
The person appointed judge should not also be the one who ate the missing biscuits.
Tell us about a small disagreement you've seen treated like a major public controversy.
A group can invent complicated rules for fairness much faster than it can agree on lunch.
Our court must decide whether arriving 'in five minutes' actually means fifteen. What's the evidence?
Who would give the most convincing closing argument about why pineapple belongs on pizza?
A trial by blind taste test or a jury made up entirely of people's grandparents?
All silly courtroom disputes should end with everyone sharing the disputed snack.
What two ordinary activities could be combined to create a sport nobody asked for?
Our Olympic event involves carrying a full cup of tea through a maze. What should the rules be?
Competitive pillow stacking or synchronised shopping-trolley steering?
The person explaining an invented sport always becomes suspiciously good at its rules.
An international championship for folding fitted sheets would humble the world's greatest athletes.
Tell us about a childhood game that became extremely competitive for no sensible reason.
Your group invents a sport played with three balloons and a laundry basket. What counts as a goal?
Which group member would argue most fiercely over the official equipment specifications?
A slow-motion race where the last person wins or an obstacle course completed while telling jokes?
A sport cannot truly succeed until somebody gets disqualified for an incredibly minor offence.
We inherit a peaceful kingdom with no money but an enormous supply of carrots. What's our first policy?
Who in this group would make a surprisingly good ruler of a town of fifty people?
A kingdom where everyone gets a pet goose or one where every official announcement comes as a poem?
Our royal council would spend its first afternoon choosing unnecessarily elaborate titles.
Tell us about a time a small group made running a simple event look like governing a nation.
A royal banquet run by friends always has one person trying to redesign the seating chart.
The people demand a national symbol and our only options are a spoon or a sandal. Which wins?
What ridiculously minor issue could bring down our imaginary government?
Being the royal keeper of maps or the official tester of the palace mattresses?
A constitutional monarchy based on group-chat polls would be the least efficient government imaginable.
Gravity becomes half as strong every Tuesday. What everyday object becomes the biggest nuisance?
What would be the funniest practical consequence if everybody could jump exactly three metres high?
A world where rain falls sideways or one where objects bounce slightly whenever you put them down?
Floating furniture would sound wonderful until someone tried serving soup.
Tell us about a real science fact that sounded made up the first time you heard it.
A world with extremely slow falling leaves would turn autumn into a patience test.
For one day shadows can move independently. Whose shadow gets us into trouble?
Which everyday sport would change the most if balls moved in slow motion?
Being able to carry enormously heavy objects easily or walking on ceilings without feeling upside down?
The worst superpower for a messy roommate would be making every dropped item roll uphill.
A little shop sells bottled emotions but labels keep falling off. What happens when we try to buy excitement?
What magical item would you expect to find behind the counter of an otherwise ordinary corner shop?
A notebook that draws your day as a comic or a clock that adds ten extra minutes to afternoon naps?
Any magical shop with a loyalty card should be treated with considerable suspicion.
Tell us about a tiny shop that felt as though it belonged in a storybook.
The shopkeeper who knows exactly what everyone wants is either very observant or deeply magical.
Every purchase comes with a harmless temporary curse. What item would still tempt us?
Who here would accidentally buy a talking umbrella and then argue with it all the way home?
A shopping bag that never tears or a pair of shoes that always lead you to the nearest bakery?
The truly magical purchase would be an umbrella nobody ever leaves on public transport.
What subject would make school considerably more interesting if it existed only one day a week?
Our school timetable includes Advanced Queueing and Practical Snack Sharing. Who becomes top of the class?
A lesson on talking to plants or a class in designing wildly impractical furniture?
Even in a school for ridiculous subjects, somebody would worry about the final exam.
The most useful compulsory course might be how to recover gracefully after calling a teacher by the wrong name.
Tell us about a real school activity that felt like an accidental comedy competition.
We have to teach a subject using only mime. Which teacher makes the class completely confused?
What homework assignment would be so enjoyable nobody needed reminding to do it?
A school with no desks but lots of workshops or one where every class ends with a quiz written by students?
An imaginary university should award degrees in surviving a group project without losing friendships.
Archaeologists in the year 3000 discover a tangled drawer of charging cables. What do they think it was used for?
What ordinary object from today would confuse historians who knew nothing about our habits?
Future people interpreting a remote control as a musical instrument or a selfie stick as ceremonial equipment?
A museum exhibition about our old group chats would need more explanation than an ancient language dictionary.
Tell us about finding an outdated gadget and struggling to remember how people used it.
A perfectly normal supermarket receipt might look like an elaborate social document to a visitor from the future.
A historian finds six mismatched socks in a drawer and concludes they were a family crest. What do we say?
Which embarrassing internet habit should future generations definitely never discover?
Leaving behind a detailed diary of an ordinary day or a box full of mystery objects without labels?
The best thing to put in a time capsule is a clear explanation of why people owned so many water bottles.
All the furniture forms a band when nobody is looking. Which item gets the drum solo?
If the objects in this room formed a choir, what would the loudest one sing about?
A trumpet made from a watering can or a violin played by a very determined umbrella?
An orchestra of household appliances would be excellent if the blender agreed to play softly.
Tell us about making an improvised musical instrument out of something completely unexpected.
The kitchen drawer probably contains enough rattling objects for a percussion section.
Our band of household objects books its first performance. What's the biggest technical problem?
Who would insist on becoming manager of a group whose lead singer is a kettle?
A refrigerator performing dramatic opera or a desk fan producing experimental electronic music?
A band featuring a microwave would have to limit its songs to the length of a reheating cycle.
If your breakfast choices determined your daily job, which meal would lead to the strangest career?
Everyone wakes up to find cereal has become the world's main currency. How do we pay for transport?
A café serving breakfast at midnight or one where customers must invent their own pancake shape?
A breakfast buffet should never be trusted to settle international diplomatic disputes.
Tell us about a time a simple breakfast became the start of an unexpectedly eventful day.
The person who says they never eat breakfast often has surprisingly strong opinions about breakfast foods.
An alien asks our group to explain why one food is considered breakfast and another dinner. Who tries first?
What would be the most absurd official title for the person in charge of breakfast?
Porridge that changes colour with your mood or toast that prints a tiny weather forecast?
The only truly fair breakfast rule is letting people decide when their morning starts.
Our group becomes famous because a pigeon steals the microphone during a video. Who gives the interview?
What harmless accident would make the funniest reason for a group to appear on the news?
Being known for rescuing a runaway shopping trolley or inventing a surprisingly popular handshake?
Accidental celebrities should be allowed to give only one interview before returning to normal life.
Tell us about a moment when an ordinary person accidentally became the centre of attention.
Someone who goes viral for a silly dance will inevitably be asked to recreate it at family events for years.
A magazine asks us for the secret behind our sudden fame. How long before somebody invents a ridiculous origin story?
Which person here would take charge of our imaginary public image despite having no experience?
Fifteen minutes of fame with a ridiculous nickname or a tiny local award nobody outside your street understands?
The funniest celebrity endorsement would be a person who became famous for making an excellent sandwich.
